methodological_rigor.justification: The study is a descriptive in vitro characterization using organotypic raft cultures of HPV16-transfected tonsil keratinocytes, with primary untransfected tonsil raft cultures serving as a reasonable comparator and multiple male/female donor lines included (Methods 2.1–2.6; Results 3.2). However, the manuscript reports no biological or technical replicate counts for the immunofluorescence panels, no quantification of staining intensity, no statistical tests, no error bars/CIs, and no power consideration — findings are presented as qualitative patterns across passages (Results 3.3–3.5). Blinded scoring of histology/IF, sample-size justification, and formal titer statistics are absent, and the qPCR titer data (Figure 2) are described without reported variance or inferential statistics. The design is appropriate for a model-development paper but the analytic rigor is limited and the single anomalous line (M19) is explained post hoc by referring to a previous publication rather than analyzed prospectively.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical in vitro model-development study using transfected human keratinocytes in 3D raft culture, which maps to Oxford LoE 5 (mechanistic/basic science). Clinical relevance is plausible but indirect: HPV+ OPSCC is a rising, clinically important malignancy with real unmet need for early-detection biomarkers (Introduction), and a tractable 3D model recapitulating integration, differentiation loss, and marker shifts (p16, K8, p120, COX5B) could support downstream biomarker and therapeutic work. However, no patient-level endpoints (OS, PFS, diagnostic accuracy) are generated, no novel biomarker is validated against patient samples here, and translational pathway from this model to clinical screening remains speculative.

reporting_quality.justification: No single checklist fits perfectly (there are no animals or patients enrolled as a cohort); ARRIVE is the closest biomedical standard applicable to a preclinical experimental model, and reporting is partial — reagents, antibodies with catalog numbers, cell culture conditions and raft protocol are described in reasonable detail (Methods 2.1–2.6), but replicates, blinding of scoring, randomization of samples, pre-specified outcomes, and quantitative image-analysis pipelines are not reported. IRB number for discarded tonsil samples is given (IRB# 25284), which is appropriate. No data-availability or code-availability statement is present in the manuscript as provided; no repository, accession number, or supplementary data link is cited beyond a referenced Table S1 of primers, so reproducibility posture is weak.

novelty_literature.justification: Organotypic raft culture for HPV life-cycle study is a long-established method, including from the authors' own prior work in cervical, foreskin, and tonsil keratinocytes (refs 23, 24, 26, 70, 71, 77, 81), and HPV16 integration-associated marker shifts (p16 up, p53/pRb down, K8 up) are well described in the literature cited. The novelty is incremental: a longitudinal, multi-passage characterization of HPV16-transfected tonsil raft cultures across differentiation, integration, and metabolic markers in one coordinated panel, with male/female donor comparison. The 'first' claim for a 3D in vitro model of HPV16-associated OPSCC progression (Discussion) is weakened by the authors' own prior tonsil raft publications (ref 71 explicitly compares HPV16 replication in tonsil vs. foreskin) and by independent tonsil organotypic work (ref 80).

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized in standard IMRaD and generally readable, with clear topic sentences and systematic walk-throughs of each marker (Results 3.3–3.5). Weaknesses: the abstract is duplicated — a narrative paragraph is followed by a structured Background/Methods/Results/Conclusions version — which is redundant; the Introduction and Discussion restate the clinical rationale (lateral neck mass, cost figures, screening limitations) several times; several figure callouts reference panels and passage numbers densely in-text without visuals available for review, making standalone interpretation difficult. Terminology is appropriate and acronyms are generally defined on first use, though some minor typos appear (e.g., 'biochemical differentiation expression patterns', 'HPV16E2 5′' primer in text).

key_strengths: Clinically important question (rising HPV16-associated OPSCC with no validated early-detection platform) addressed with an established, biologically faithful 3D organotypic raft system
Coordinated multi-marker characterization across differentiation (K5, K10, K6), carcinogenesis (K8, p16, p53, pRb), adhesion (p120), and metabolism (COX5B) in a single model
Inclusion of both male and female donor-derived HPV16 tonsil keratinocyte lines, with internal cross-reference to prior integration/structural-variant analyses (ref 34)
Methods for raft production, HPV16 electroporation, viral titering, and IF staining are described in reasonable experimental detail with reagent/catalog identifiers
key_concerns: Descriptive design with no quantification of IF signal, no replicate counts reported, no statistical analysis, and no blinded scoring — limiting evidentiary strength
Novelty is incremental; the authors' own prior work and independent reports already describe HPV16 tonsil raft systems and the integration-associated marker shifts shown here (refs 70, 71, 80, 81)
No data- or code-availability statement, no repository deposition, and no supplementary data beyond a referenced primer table — reproducibility posture is weak
Duplicated abstract and repeated clinical-rationale passages across Introduction and Discussion inflate length without adding content
M19 outlier line is explained post hoc via a prior publication rather than prospectively analyzed, and sample sizes (number of donor lines, replicates per passage) are not clearly stated
Translational claim (improved early-detection biomarkers) is aspirational — no biomarker is independently validated against patient OPSCC samples in this manuscript
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently executed but largely descriptive and incremental in vitro model-characterization paper with no quantitative statistics and limited reproducibility support; appropriate for a Tier 3 preclinical/translational journal after major revisions addressing quantification, replicates, and data availability.
